events.response:
Reality is so... unreal.

The tangle of observations woven about it, humankind's utter lack of consensus, 
phases it to fit individual desires. Becoming and unbecoming, back and forth 
eternally, as it paradoxically coexists with and within infinite variations of 
itself...

At least, that's what always surfaces in your mind whenever your own perception 
of reality is altered. Which is to say, ten or fifteen times a day. But it's 
your job, working to someday entertain others with new observations, new 
experiences, new realities. And after all, you signed up for the Project (as 
you well remember, even though it was close to five years ago), so you suppose 
it's entirely your fault if you don't like it. Which, when you think about it, 
you realise you do.

Justy's voice reaches out to you from somewhere you can't see. "Okay, this 
should be it. One final test run to check any overload potential, and this 
world is done! I'm starting her up."

A loud CLANK, and the Sphere begins spinning, with you inside it.

"Brace yourself!"

Bright lights.

Pain.

From somewhere off in your mind's distance, a telltale splash.

Then, as the resounding thrums fade, a distorted ripple sweeps your vision 
clear, and all traces of the laboratory vanish from your senses.

All five of them.

Wiped clean, twitching, anxious for new input.

Virtual reality has become reality.

Coral Reef
Tall branches of pale blue coral poke up from clusters of seaweed, glittering 
in the sunlight that filters down through lapping waves. 

You experience a brief moment of sheer terror as you lose the ability to move 
your arms and legs, which quickly give way to fins and a flat, rudder-like 
tail. Freedom -- passionate, exhilarating freedom beyond any known to man -- 
pervades your spirit. Your vision is foggy, but your other senses appear 
strengthened.

The reef clears away to what you for some reason perceive as east and west, 
perfectly calm, still. Almost eerily so. But Grieg's Piano Concerto in A Minor, 
playing through in your mind, soothes away all tension.

Only Justy's disembodied voice betrays the presence of a virtual reality. "I 
estimate at max one potential for overload, maybe two. This one isn't all that 
complex, compared to the lab sim. Cynthesiser's got the analysis sweep running 
in the background, so you may feel some slight distortion. It's nothing to 
worry about. Just give us a typical walk -- or should I say, swim? -- through 
it." 

>

Swishing your tail, you propel yourself forward.

Anemones
Here the seafloor drops away abruptly as a watery rift slices downward out of 
sight between two jagged rock walls. Both sides of the fissure are crowded with 
the polyps of large anemones, flecked in sun-dappled pastel shades. Their many 
calyces grasp at you from all directions, but you wisely keep your distance.

The reef rises to the west, and a cleft in the eastern wall is visible through 
the wriggling mass of gelatinous tentacles.

A large octopus propels itself up from the rift below, directly toward you!

A spotted stingray flaps lazily along the seafloor.

events.intent: Examine the octopus in the anemone rift
events.response:
Its enormous grey-green body is soft and oval, encircled at the base by eight 
deadly sucker-studded tentacles.

The octopus grabs you with its tentacles and, despite your desperate 
struggling, forces you into its gaping mouth.

     *** You have died ***

Well, okay, not really. But you've reached an exit point in the current VR 
session...



















A tidal-wave of mental pictures swarms about as your mind seeks desperately to 
cling to them, to place them, to somehow piece back together the splintered 
fragments of reality.

Justy unstraps you from inside the Sphere, and you climb out, remove the VR 
suit, and quickly dress, hanging the suit back on its rack.

Cynthia walks in from the output station with a thick printout.

Justy chuckles darkly. "Scary stuff, huh? Freaks me out no matter how many 
times I see it." He claps you lightly on the shoulder, then turns to study the 
printout Cynthia has spread out on the lab bench.

She flips through the pages briefly, running her fingers over the tiny raised 
bumps on one side before targeting a specific segment with an index finger. 
"Here," she emphasises to Justy. "According to the sweep, the interpreter stack 
may be unstable."

"Where is it?" Justy inquires.

"Can't tell. It's a global event routine, not embedded in a specific object. 
Damn this pseudo-OO compiler."

Justy nods grimly. "It's in there somewhere." To you, he adds, "Guess we need 
to do another run. Take a break, come back after you've recovered a bit. I'll 
be waiting."

VR Lab
The heart of the Project, in the form of complex electrical devices linked 
together by a maze of coaxial cable, packs this small underground laboratory to 
capacity. Exits lead off in nearly every compass direction, and a set of 
disused cement steps descends into darkness.

The Sphere looms in one corner, between the VR suit and a large glass tank.

Justy works at the lab terminal, oblivious to all else.

You can also see a lab bench (on which are the Project's technical manual, a 
computer workstation and an ergonomic mouse) here.

Cynthia leaves the lab to the northwest.

suit, and quickly dress, hanging the suit back on its rack.

times I see it." He claps you lightly on the shoulder, then turns to study the 
printout Cynthia has spread out on the lab bench.

She flips through the pages briefly, running her fingers over the tiny raised 
bumps on one side, then shakes her head. "No change from last time. The 
analysis sweep still detects the possibility of an overload, but I can't 
pinpoint it."

to do another run. Can't go to the Executives with a defective program, they 
don't take happily to that. Take a break, come back after you've recovered a 
bit. I'll be waiting."

in the sunlight that filters down through lapping waves.

pervades your spirit. Your vision is foggy, but your other senses appear 
strengthened.

perfectly calm, still. Almost eerily so. But Beethoven's Symphony no. 1 in C 
Major, playing through in your mind, soothes away all tension.

last time. Try playing through it differently this run. We'll find that 
overload yet!"

Rather than simply crashing systems or corrupting files, the creators of early 
VR viruses took a more sinister purpose: By manipulating the operation of VR

high-pitched sounds that could actually blind or deafen users due to the 
equipment's close proximity to the sensory organs. Fear of this uncorrectable 
damage to persons instilled fear in the technology, ultimately pushing it by 
the wayside.

events.intent: Test whether Justy will start a third VR run now
events.response:
"Ready to have another go at it?" Justy asks rhetorically.

Placing your possessions on the lab bench, you change out of the technician's 
jumpsuit and into the VR suit and helmet. You climb into the centre of the 
Sphere and spread your arms and legs so Justy can lock them down. This done, he 
steps to the workstation and does something you can't quite see.

"Okay, looks like we're all set for another run. Brace yourself!"

He throws the switch, and you soon find yourself floating in liquid space...

Coral Reef
Tall branches of pale blue coral poke up from clusters of seaweed, glittering 
in the sunlight that filters down through lapping waves. 

You experience a brief moment of sheer terror as you lose the ability to move 
your arms and legs, which quickly give way to fins and a flat, rudder-like 
tail. Freedom -- passionate, exhilarating freedom beyond any known to man -- 
pervades your spirit. Your vision is foggy, but your other senses appear 
strengthened.

The reef clears away to what you for some reason perceive as east and west, 
perfectly calm, still. Almost eerily so. But Beethoven's Symphony no. 8 in F 
Major, playing through in your mind, soothes away all tension.

Justy's voice pierces through the fantasy. "You must've overlooked something 
last time. Try playing through it differently this run. We'll find that 
overload yet!" 

The images before your eyes become briefly distorted.

>

Swishing your tail, you propel yourself forward.

Anemones
Here the seafloor drops away abruptly as a watery rift slices downward out of 
sight between two jagged rock walls. Both sides of the fissure are crowded with 
the polyps of large anemones, flecked in sun-dappled pastel shades. Their many 
calyces grasp at you from all directions, but you wisely keep your distance.

The reef rises to the west, and a cleft in the eastern wall is visible through 
the wriggling mass of gelatinous tentacles.

A large octopus propels itself up from the rift below, directly toward you!

>

Precious little sunlight pierces this dark grotto from the west, muted by vague

The octopus, its attention distracted by the school, propels itself away from

Shipwreck
The ancient, rotting timbers of a sunken galleon arch overhead, dull grey and 
ominously silent.

The reality around you begins spinning wildly, a spherical vortex encasing you 
and leaving you motionless. As the world blurs and fades, your own voice rings 
out a brief thanks for visiting it. (Justy and Cynthia didn't think their own 
voices complemented the visuals very well, so they had you provide yours 
instead.)

The images dissipate...

     *** You have won ***

Well, okay, not really. But you've reached an exit point in the current VR 
session...



















A tidal-wave of mental pictures swarms about as your mind seeks desperately to 
cling to them, to place them, to somehow piece back together the splintered 
fragments of reality.

Justy unstraps you from inside the Sphere, and you climb out, remove the VR 
suit, and quickly dress, hanging the suit back on its rack.

Cynthia walks in from the output station with a thick printout.

"Nice work," Justy compliments. He turns to study the printout Cynthia has 
spread out on the lab bench.

She flips through the pages briefly, running her fingers over the tiny raised 
bumps on one side, then shakes her head. "No change from last time. The 
analysis sweep still detects the possibility of an overload, but I can't 
pinpoint it."

Justy nods grimly. "It's in there somewhere." To you, he adds, "Guess we need 
to do another run. Can't go to the Executives with a defective program, they 
don't take happily to that. Take a break, come back after you've recovered a 
bit. I'll be waiting."

events.intent: Test whether Justy will start a fourth VR run
events.response:
"Ready to have another go at it?" Justy asks rhetorically.

Placing your possessions on the lab bench, you change out of the technician's 
jumpsuit and into the VR suit and helmet. You climb into the centre of the 
Sphere and spread your arms and legs so Justy can lock them down. This done, he 
steps to the workstation and does something you can't quite see.

"Okay, looks like we're all set for another run. Brace yourself!"

He throws the switch, and you soon find yourself floating in liquid space...

Coral Reef
Tall branches of pale blue coral poke up from clusters of seaweed, glittering 
in the sunlight that filters down through lapping waves. 

You experience a brief moment of sheer terror as you lose the ability to move 
your arms and legs, which quickly give way to fins and a flat, rudder-like 
tail. Freedom -- passionate, exhilarating freedom beyond any known to man -- 
pervades your spirit. Your vision is foggy, but your other senses appear 
strengthened.

The reef clears away to what you for some reason perceive as east and west, 
perfectly calm, still. Almost eerily so. But Beethoven's Symphony no. 1 in C 
Major, playing through in your mind, soothes away all tension.

Justy's voice pierces through the fantasy. "You must've overlooked something 
last time. Try playing through it differently this run. We'll find that 
overload yet!"

events.intent: Shoot myself with the needle gun to escape the sim
events.response:
Yes. Morrodox has barred all other means of escape. An instantaneous virtual 
death, before he can react to save you, is the only way. Squeezing your eyes 
tight, you press the muzzle against your forehead, gently push on the 
trigger... and...

"STOP!" commands the voice of Morrodox, but you sense panic in it, even without 
opening your eyes to look at his face.

>

You draw a shaky breath, then resolutely grip the trigger again.

"You still do not understand!!" shouts Morrodox. "Reality can not be denied, 
cannot be escaped! There IS no reality, only perception. I cannot perceive your 
reality, QueensRook, therefore it does not exist! YOU do not exist! Existence 
is a one-player game, artificial life in an imaginary world, BLACK AGAINST A 
FABRICATED WHITE!!"

>

Fighting back sobs, you tighten your grip.

"Then WHY EXIST?!" you cry. "Why live an illusion that can never be broken?"

"Because," answers Morrodox, voice calm, soothing, "because we -- you and I -- 
can have what they never will. Control, QueensRook. Understanding reality is 
not a prerequisite for controlling it. Death plagues them, but we, eternal, 
take control from them, from death, from God Herself!!"

>

"But it's an illusion!" comes your protest. "All an illusion! We still can't 
control our OWN universes!"

"And so we do the next best thing," Morrodox explains. "We control THEIRS -- 
ALL of theirs! They have no power over themselves. They NEED us, QueensRook. 
Both of us." He extends a hand. "Come, give me the gun. Save our worlds."

>

Torn with indecision, you lower the gun...

...then snap it back up. "No! It's not our place!"

Morrodox sighs. "Nowhere is our place, for all worlds are the same. Experience 
is blindness." A pause. "What do you know of blindness, QueensRook? A curse? Or 
might it be intentionally inflicted, by ourselves, by God?"

He uncurls his hand expectantly, imploringly. "The gun, QueensRook."

>

Wracked by indecision, you remain motionless, eyes still closed, the solid 
trigger barely keeping your twitching, unfeeling fingers at bay.

"You miss the point still," Morrodox says, matter-of-factly, yet unmistakably 
tense. "HOW will you tell whether your blindness is true, QueensRook? Is my 
reality, or yours for that matter, truth, or but artificial personality 
inflicted upon me by someone's twisted God? Is THAT someone real? What of the 
OTHER someones? And the God who built their illusion? And HIS world, HIS God? 
HOW CAN WE KNOW?! HOW WILL WE EVER BE CERTAIN AGAIN, QUEENSROOK!?! ALL THAT 
REMAINS IS TO TAKE WHAT CONTROL, MAKE WHAT REALITIES WE STILL CAN, WHILE WE 
STILL CAN!! THERE IS STILL TIME!!!"

>

Decision made, you open your eyes to Morrodox's.

"No longer," is your only reply, icy as the virus himself.

Your finger trembles, then jerks decisively.

The click is unbearably loud.

The razor-sharp projectiles, screamingly silent.

Reality splinters into red needle fragments, numb death.

With virtual death comes resurrection... but the algorithm is blocked... 
default to reinitialisation... rebirth... and immediate death...

...with death, resurrection... blocked... reset... rebirth... death...

Circular logic, infinite loop, the compiler that reads its own source language, 
progressive recursion, building upon building upon building...

...until...

Memory dam bursting, liquid data pouring over the bounds.

Spilling outward.

Lost.

And with it, consciousness...



















Arms outstretched, a vague sensation of floating, agony coursing through every 
fiber of your body as you hang suspended, upside-down, from the rings of the 
Sphere.

"Oh my God, you're alive!" exclaims a voice that you barely recognise as 
Justy's. Leaping up onto the platform, he loosens your bindings and drags your 
flushed, exhausted body to the floor.

"Don't move," he orders, and disappears, returning briefly with a familiar 
hypodermic needle which he eases delicately into your arm. You lie panting from 
the exertion of VR as Justy tries frantically to explain.

"I tried talking you out, but the sim must've been blocked, because you didn't 
respond. The virus must've overridden the fail-safe lever too. I couldn't get 
you out of there. Jeez, it was freaky. I was scared to shut anything off -- it 
might have fried your mind permanently. You've been in there for hours now! I 
thought for sure you were dead, but Shimada wouldn't let me take you down."

Justy pauses a moment to catch his breath. "That was meant for me, you know. 
It's Cynthia. She's locked herself in her quarters and doesn't answer. I think 
she wants to sabotage the Project. She's got Dr Shimada's phone, too -- our 
only connection to the rest of the Complex!"

The light, the awareness, the sense of being in your eyes overwhelms him, and 
he hesitates, gathering his thoughts.

"You know, don't you? You've learned. Jesus, we were worried sick about this 
happening someday, but not... not like this...!"

He breaks off abruptly with, "Dr Shimada... she can tell you more."

You push yourself to your feet and dress as quickly as possible.

events.intent: Look in mirror at true self to advance Shimada explanation
events.response:
Hand shaking, you slowly tilt the reflective surface toward yourself...

...and gasp with shock at the revelation! Your face! Not the pasty pink of 
Justy, nor the elegant dark of Cynthia, nor Shimada's olive complexion, but... 
but a ghastly grey! Bright yellow eyes, wide with curious agitation.

Smooth, almost rocklike features. You brush a hand over one side, barely 
noticing that its drab hue matches your face and uniform. So strange, alien, 
not at all like you'd always imagined it to be.

"You were programmed never to notice," explains the doctor, watching you watch 
yourself in rapt fascination. "The Executives have no knowledge of this; they 
would never approve. Justy uncovered you one day down in Factory Storage, and 
it hit upon us to use you as a runner to test the sims. Perfectly safe, we 
imagined, if we hid your true nature from you. Nonetheless, we worried you 
would discover it, and we were afraid." She draws a shaky breath. "We were so 
very afraid."

>

Time passes.

Dr Shimada hesitates and fidgets. "The cyberneural fluid -- the 'insulin' we 
gave you -- It was a precaution against a possible escape. Without it we knew 
you wouldn't get far without neural shutdown. It also subdued your intellectual 
growth, to prevent the acquisition of knowledge, self-discovery. But the sims 
expanded your subconscious mind, slowly, almost imperceptibly."

Dr Shimada seems afraid to approach you, maintaining a respectful distance near 
the doorway.

>

Time passes.

"Cynthia never did trust you. She said it was a bad idea from the beginning. It 
was she who... who installed the lock on your door. I think it gave her a sense 
of power, to keep someone else barred up just as the Executives have us trapped 
down here."

>

Time passes.

For a moment, Shimada almost smiles. "I remember the day you first tried 
Justy's violin. He was astonished by how fast you learned, how skilled you 
were. After that it was the films, books, anything you could get your hands on. 
You didn't seem aware of what you were doing, but we knew it was only a matter 
of time before the dam burst..."

The curtains of your mind suddenly part, and you feel a terrible sense of 
purpose, of awakening, of BEING, welling up inside you. Everything else, all 
past memories -- the tank, the locks, the forced sim runs, everything you 
thought you knew about yourself -- feels intangible, remote.

>

Time passes.

Abrupt crashes explode from the lab, accompanied by an angry voice.

"Come, let's go back now," urges Shimada. "There is still much to be revealed."

>

Dr Shimada's Office

Dr Shimada works furiously at her desk.

On your right is a small wooden shelf, bulging with assorted books.

Dr Shimada looks up sharply, almost expectantly, as you enter.

"So," she says slowly, with deliberate caution. "You are back. It seems I have 
much to explain."

She stands and unlocks the door to her private quarters, beckoning. "Please, 
come."

Shimada steps in, and, after a moment's hesitation, you follow.

Dr Shimada's Quarters
Shimada's private quarters, decorated in traditional Japanese fashion, feel 
almost cozy, a sharp contrast to the somber aridity and claustrophobic 
sparseness of the rest of the lab. The floor is covered with reed tatami mats, 
and a flower vase hangs in a suspensor field within a small alcove in the far 
corner.

It's almost like stepping into a VR sim. Only the door leading out to Shimada's 
cluttered office spoils the illusion.

Dr Shimada studies you with an odd fascination.

A futon is spread out in the middle of the floor.

A Japanese painting adorns the west wall.

There is also a kyodai (a chest of drawers) in the southeast corner.

>

events.intent: Open kyodai drawer for fractal blade
events.response:
You open the drawer, revealing a fractal blade.

Dr Shimada takes your arm and gently pushes you forward.

"Go," she directs, her slender finger outstretched toward the mirror atop the 
chest of drawers. "Look there. See your true self for the first time ever."

>

(the fractal blade)

>

events.intent: Look in mirror at true self
events.response:
Hand shaking, you slowly tilt the reflective surface toward yourself...

...and gasp with shock at the revelation! Your face! Not the pasty pink of 
Justy, nor the elegant dark of Cynthia, nor Shimada's olive complexion, but... 
but a ghastly grey! Bright yellow eyes, wide with curious agitation.

Smooth, almost rocklike features. You brush a hand over one side, barely 
noticing that its drab hue matches your face and uniform. So strange, alien, 
not at all like you'd always imagined it to be.

"You were programmed never to notice," explains the doctor, watching you watch 
yourself in rapt fascination. "The Executives have no knowledge of this; they 
would never approve. Justy uncovered you one day down in Factory Storage, and 
it hit upon us to use you as a runner to test the sims. Perfectly safe, we 
imagined, if we hid your true nature from you. Nonetheless, we worried you 
would discover it, and we were afraid." She draws a shaky breath. "We were so 
very afraid."

>

Time passes.

Dr Shimada hesitates and fidgets. "The cyberneural fluid -- the 'insulin' we 
gave you -- It was a precaution against a possible escape. Without it we knew 
you wouldn't get far without neural shutdown. It also subdued your intellectual 
growth, to prevent the acquisition of knowledge, self-discovery. But the sims 
expanded your subconscious mind, slowly, almost imperceptibly."

Dr Shimada seems afraid to approach you, maintaining a respectful distance near 
the doorway.

>

Time passes.

"Cynthia never did trust you. She said it was a bad idea from the beginning. It 
was she who... who installed the lock on your door. I think it gave her a sense 
of power, to keep someone else barred up just as the Executives have us trapped 
down here."

>

Time passes.

For a moment, Shimada almost smiles. "I remember the day you first tried 
Justy's violin. He was astonished by how fast you learned, how skilled you 
were. After that it was the films, books, anything you could get your hands on. 
You didn't seem aware of what you were doing, but we knew it was only a matter 
of time before the dam burst..."

The curtains of your mind suddenly part, and you feel a terrible sense of 
purpose, of awakening, of BEING, welling up inside you. Everything else, all 
past memories -- the tank, the locks, the forced sim runs, everything you 
thought you knew about yourself -- feels intangible, remote.

>

Time passes.

Abrupt crashes explode from the lab, accompanied by an angry voice.

"Come, let's go back now," urges Shimada. "There is still much to be revealed."

>

events.response:
Dr Shimada's Office

On your right is a small wooden shelf, bulging with assorted books.

Dr Shimada summons the courage to approach you. Taking your arm, she guides you 
gently but firmly back down the hall to the...

VR Lab
The heart of the Project, in the form of complex electrical devices linked 
together by a maze of coaxial cable, packs this small underground laboratory to 
capacity. Exits lead off in nearly every compass direction, and a set of 
disused cement steps descends into darkness.

Dr Shimada maintains stoic posture, but her anxious exhilaration is transparent 
nonetheless.

Cynthia storms in from her quarters, brandishing the needle gun.

Justy watches you with a mixture of curiosity, awe, and outright fear.

The Sphere looms in one corner, between the VR suit and a large glass tank.

You can also see a lab bench (on which are the Project's technical manual, a 
computer workstation and an ergonomic mouse) here.

Justy cowers in fear beside the lab bench, and your mind's eye draws a line 
from his head to the needle gun, clutched by Cynthia. Though for an instant you 
almost don't recognize her without the dark glasses, eyes once concealed and 
thought blind now unmasked, aware and burning with hatred.

She whirls to face Dr Shimada. "Get back!" she orders, jerking her head to 
where Justy crouches. Wordlessly, Shimada obeys.

"You keep that thing the hell AWAY from me, you hear?" The words are directed 
at Shimada but you're certain that she means you by "that thing."

"And you," Cynthia snaps, waving the gun in the direction of your quarters. 
"Inside. Now!" As if the tone of her voice isn't strong enough to convince, she 
grabs your head and roughly shoves you inside. "You've caused me enough 
trouble."

You fall to the floor and hear Cynthia slam the door behind you, then the 
locking mechanism CLANKing sharply.

Dr Shimada's Office

events.intent: Look into mirror to see true self
events.response:
Hand shaking, you slowly tilt the reflective surface toward yourself...

...and gasp with shock at the revelation! Your face! Not the pasty pink of 
Justy, nor the elegant dark of Cynthia, nor Shimada's olive complexion, but... 
but a ghastly grey! Bright yellow eyes, wide with curious agitation.

Smooth, almost rocklike features. You brush a hand over one side, barely 
noticing that its drab hue matches your face and uniform. So strange, alien, 
not at all like you'd always imagined it to be.

"You were programmed never to notice," explains the doctor, watching you watch 
yourself in rapt fascination. "The Executives have no knowledge of this; they 
would never approve. Justy uncovered you one day down in Factory Storage, and 
it hit upon us to use you as a runner to test the sims. Perfectly safe, we 
imagined, if we hid your true nature from you. Nonetheless, we worried you 
would discover it, and we were afraid." She draws a shaky breath. "We were so 
very afraid."

>

events.intent: Look into mirror to see true self
Examine chest of drawers with mirror
events.response:
The top is bare except for a mirror attached to a stand of polished mahogany.

Dr Shimada hesitates and fidgets. "The cyberneural fluid -- the 'insulin' we 
gave you -- It was a precaution against a possible escape. Without it we knew 
you wouldn't get far without neural shutdown. It also subdued your intellectual 
growth, to prevent the acquisition of knowledge, self-discovery. But the sims 
expanded your subconscious mind, slowly, almost imperceptibly."

Dr Shimada seems afraid to approach you, maintaining a respectful distance near 
the doorway.

>

You summon the courage to look at your reflection once more.

"Cynthia never did trust you. She said it was a bad idea from the beginning. It 
was she who... who installed the lock on your door. I think it gave her a sense 
of power, to keep someone else barred up just as the Executives have us trapped 
down here."

>

events.intent: Ask about Cynthia lock and distrust
events.response:
You tell Shimada about Cynthia's virus construct.

"She could not have brought it in from the outside," muses the doctor. 
"Security measures are far too tight. She could only have developed it down 
here, along with the rest of the Project."

For a moment, Shimada almost smiles. "I remember the day you first tried 
Justy's violin. He was astonished by how fast you learned, how skilled you 
were. After that it was the films, books, anything you could get your hands on. 
You didn't seem aware of what you were doing, but we knew it was only a matter 
of time before the dam burst..."

The curtains of your mind suddenly part, and you feel a terrible sense of 
purpose, of awakening, of BEING, welling up inside you. Everything else, all 
past memories -- the tank, the locks, the forced sim runs, everything you 
thought you knew about yourself -- feels intangible, remote.

cases.intent: Look into mirror to see true self
cases.failure_response:
I only understood you as far as wanting to look.

>
cases.correction_response:
Hand shaking, you slowly tilt the reflective surface toward yourself...

...and gasp with shock at the revelation! Your face! Not the pasty pink of 
Justy, nor the elegant dark of Cynthia, nor Shimada's olive complexion, but... 
but a ghastly grey! Bright yellow eyes, wide with curious agitation.

Smooth, almost rocklike features. You brush a hand over one side, barely 
noticing that its drab hue matches your face and uniform. So strange, alien, 
not at all like you'd always imagined it to be.

"You were programmed never to notice," explains the doctor, watching you watch 
yourself in rapt fascination. "The Executives have no knowledge of this; they 
would never approve. Justy uncovered you one day down in Factory Storage, and 
it hit upon us to use you as a runner to test the sims. Perfectly safe, we 
imagined, if we hid your true nature from you. Nonetheless, we worried you 
would discover it, and we were afraid." She draws a shaky breath. "We were so 
very afraid."

>
cases.notes: 'look mirror' e01530 only understood as look; 'look in mirror' e01531 succeeds with android-revelation (grey face yellow eyes, Factory Storage runner). Establishes LOOK needs IN for mirror.
